A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRO-SCALE work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation experiments, component ablations, and appendix experiments applying PRO-SCALE to DINO and MaskCLIP.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds component controls, FPS measurements, FCCLIP results, and MaskDINO experiments.

M1.justification: Progressive token expansion, TRC, LPE, and the training losses remain unchanged. TRC moves from Section 3.1.1 to Appendix C and remains explicitly used in Section 3.1. The additional framework experiments do not document a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds joint instance-segmentation and object-detection evaluation using MaskDINO on COCO. Dataset coverage remains unchanged: COCO, Cityscapes, and ADE20K evaluation already appear in v1, including detection and open-vocabulary experiments in its appendix. FCCLIP extends model coverage within the existing open-vocabulary task.

E2.justification: The main COCO and Cityscapes comparator sets remain unchanged, but the additional comparisons expand substantially. V2 adds FCCLIP alongside MaskCLIP in Table 10, evaluates MaskDINO in Table 11, and adds Lite-DETR and RT-DETR to the previously DINO-only detection comparison in Table 8. Figure 11 also introduces qualitative comparisons against Lite-M2F and PEM.

E3.justification: V2 extends evaluation beyond computational counts to measured FPS, adds controlled component-removal settings, and introduces 50-epoch MaskDINO evaluation using mask and box AP. The detection comparison drops AP50 and combines detection AP with segmentation PQ and computational figures. Existing main-benchmark splits, training budgets, and segmentation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Table 3 adds targeted controls comparing removal of s1, progressive scaling with s1 retained, and use of LPE. Figure 11 adds comparative qualitative cases. Existing TRC, temperature, pooling, backbone, pretraining, and token-redundancy analyses are retained. Figure 10 redisplays existing configuration results rather than introducing a new configuration study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The token-similarity analysis averaged over 100 randomly selected COCO images is retained unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial FPS, component-control, FCCLIP, MaskDINO, and qualitative results while retaining the main PRO-SCALE benchmark scores. Table 2 revises PEM PQ from 61.10 to 61.07 and adds semantic and instance scores; Table 1 supplies ReMaX's previously missing 169.00 GFLOPs. MaskCLIP total GFLOPs change from 552.8/489.8 to 549.2/486.1. DINO AP remains 49.0/49.4, but v1 Table T1's AP50 and detection encoder costs of 179/126 GFLOPs disappear. V2 Table 8 uses segmentation computational figures, so these cannot establish a same-setting detection efficiency improvement.

T1.justification: The token-concatenation definitions in Equations 1–3 and TRC expression in Equation 4 are retained, with Equation 4 relocated to Appendix C. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theoretical guarantees, or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes approximately 52% encoder savings from 27% overall savings in the abstract and highlights extension to detection. Its headline contribution focuses on Mask2Former, progressive scaling, and LPE; TRC is no longer listed as a principal contribution. The central efficiency-with-competitive-segmentation claim remains unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of component controls and speed-quality trade-offs, describes LPE as weakening convolutional inductive bias, and adds a limitation attributed to ReMaX on larger models. Some new interpretations overstate their tables: Table 10 broadly claims better PQ despite FCCLIP's ADE20K decline, and Table 11 claims better mask and box AP despite lower mask AP.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, specifies LPE stride 1, identifies the existing TRC sweep configuration as (p1,1,1), and states A6000 hardware for FPS analysis. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the retained implementation. Optimizer, losses, batch size, main training schedules, and training hardware were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds the FCCLIP work and positions PRO-SCALE relative to it, while adding a specific criticism of ReMaX's applicability to larger models. Most related-work discussion remains unchanged. The additional MaskDINO bibliography entry concerns work already cited in v1 and does not establish a new research relationship.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: TRC methodology and analyses move to Appendix C, baseline details and several application/backbone studies move into the main text, and references precede the appendices. The separate supplementary title and contents pages disappear. Contributions are rewritten as prose, and the method explanation gains pixel-decoder terminology and clarification.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the main architecture figure, presents the TRC-inclusive architecture in Appendix Figure 7, and revises figure legends and configuration labels. It adds component and FPS tables, expands application tables, and adds qualitative Figure 11. New Figure 10 plots existing configuration results. Retained figures and tables are extensively rearranged and resized.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies encoder versus overall savings and adds useful controls, runtime measurements, and framework comparisons. However, Table 8 removes v1's detection-specific efficiency evidence and supports its detection discussion with segmentation computational figures. New captions also overstate gains: FCCLIP ADE20K PQ falls from 26.80 to 25.27, and MaskDINO mask AP falls from 46.00 to 45.66. These material reporting regressions coexist with stronger empirical coverage, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
